priority_blocker_addressed.claim: Godot production runtime needs real InputMap drive + save/load + pause freeze, not gate1 JS mirror / --script smokes
priority_blocker_addressed.finding: Prior gate1/tools/core_loop_runner.mjs is a Node mirror, not Godot. Fighter.dummy_mode defaulted to 'cpu', so human P1 still ran CpuController (sticky p1_shield via Input.action_press) dual-driven with real input. Battle pause only flipped controls_enabled/BattleSim.paused — CharacterBody2D kept sliding. HitResolver never called MatchTelemetry.record_hit. CpuController._sim_aura_charge pressed shield/special without release. Fighter.try_grab() sets the OPPONENT's grabbed_by (not the grabber's), and Fighter._physics_process() unconditionally teleports any fighter with grabbed_by != null to the grab-hold offset every frame — the grab probe step only cleared the grabber's own grabbed_by, so a real (and unavoidable, input-triggered) grab-startup on fighter1 left fighter2 permanently pinned 24px from fighter1 for the rest of the match, silently defeating every later H2H repositioning and making every jab whiff.
priority_blocker_addressed.fix: ProductionGateHarness autoload boots real main scene; pause uses get_tree().paused; dummy_mode default idle + configure() clears cpu dummy for humans; HitResolver wires record_hit; CPU aura-charge releases inputs; fighter rising-edge input helpers; grab probe now awaits the physics tick that actually consumes the synthesized press before cancelling the resulting move, and clears grabbed_by on BOTH fighters (attacker and the correct opponent-side flag).
priority_blocker_addressed.real_defect_found_and_fixed: Human local-versus P1 was dual-driven by CpuController because @export dummy_mode defaulted to 'cpu' (is_cpu=false was not enough). Pause did not freeze physics. A synthesized grab input that lands one physics tick after being read/released left the *victim* fighter's grabbed_by flag set, permanently pinning it to the grabber's hold offset — a real state-leak in Fighter.gd's grab system reachable by any grab attempt that starts just as controls change hands, not just a harness artifact. Verified via production harness before/after, 6/6 stable runs.
